text:
The Blue Jackets got the kind of night Saturday that a 9-12-0 team needs. Matthew Knies and Steven Lorentz went back to Toronto, the Leafs crowd gave them an ovation, and Columbus came back in the third to win, a loss Auston Matthews called "inexcusable" (per The Leafs Nation). Knies had said the return felt "a little awkward," according to Daily Faceoff.

The season around it is harder. Columbus has scored about nine and a half fewer goals than its chances predict, the biggest gap among its problems, and at 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) the process isn't strong enough to cover for it. Conor Garland is on injured reserve, week to week, with an upper-body injury.

Zach Werenski remains the engine. He has 11 points in his last 10 games, and his pair with Damon Severson has outscored teams 18-8 at 5-on-5 even with an even share of the chances. That combination of production and losing has started trade chatter, though Yahoo reports he remains committed to the team. The Charlie Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger line has been the steadiest forward group by chances.

Our playoff odds have Columbus at 9%. What we'd watch: whether the finishing turns, because the Werenski talk will only get louder if it doesn't.
